title: EVOLVE Cima - 3,000km later.

takeaways.text: After roughly 2,800–3,200 km, including an Everesting, the retailer-presenter calls it his most comfortable road bike: it soaks up road buzz, is less harsh than a Quick Pro AR1, and had no creaks or rubbing.
Several seatpost lengths and setbacks let him dial in a small-rider fit with a slammed 140 mm stem and 34 cm bar.
Minor niggles: changing logo designs, a seatpost logo placed partly inside the frame, and an early aero bottle that was mis-moulded (replaced).
A very powerful (2,000 W+) sprinter reportedly found it not stiff enough; the presenter (about 950 W) felt no flex, and one owner preferred it to his S-Works Tarmac SL8.
His Ultegra build with 50 mm prototype wheels, aero cages, power-meter pedals and mounts weighed 6.275 kg.

disclosure: The creator says Evolve gave him the frame free and did not pay for this video. His China Cycling/Panda Podium retailer relationship remains relevant.
summary: CIMA road update after a reported 3,000 km, covering use, likes, issues and the revised build. This road platform is distinct from CIMA GR; ride impressions remain creator reports.
